about: The 20 demo payments (ADR 0003, plan D2.3/D5.1/D6.1). Transfers: real public transfers, not Clearline customers, replayed offline from recordings/. Invoices: SAMPLE COMPANY DATA (fictional), each built around a real transfer; 'why' says what was constructed. Labels come from the chain facts in provenance.json and the approved rules (docs/SPEC.md, docs/POSTING_RULES.md), never from the product's output.
split_rule: All tuning. These cases are shown in the demo and run by QA (D7.1), so none can stay unseen; a held-out set must be built separately from transfers not used here. No source transfer is in tests/real_cases_holdout.json (checked 2026-11-01); all are in the deposit tuning set tests/real_cases.json.

expected_actions.auto_match: linked to the invoice by the system and matched with no person
expected_actions.review: sent to a person to decide
expected_actions.flag: can never pay the invoice; the problem is named

scenarios.title: Short by 0.000117 (inside the approved 0.01 rounding line)

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: Short by 0.000117, at most 0.01: POSTING_RULES R3d (decision 3, Approved) closes the invoice with one rounding line of 0.01 or less. Constructed: the sample invoice amount was set 0.000117 above the real transfer.
label.expected_reason: Paid: 2,495.499883 USDT against 2,495.50; the 0.000117 difference is within the 0.01 rounding line.

scenarios.known_gap: The matcher today treats any shortfall as 'short' and sends it to a person; the 0.01 rounding tolerance is planned in D5.4 (approval-only, posting). Not changed in this PR.

scenarios.title: Short by 8.74 (0.9%), accepted short by a person

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: Short by 8.74181, above 0.01: only a person may accept a shortfall (POSTING_RULES C2/C7). Constructed: invoice set above the real transfer.
label.expected_reason: Short by 8.74 USDT (0.9%), likely a fee deducted before sending. A person decides; here they accept it as settled.

person_decision.note: SAMPLE: customer's exchange deducted its withdrawal fee; accepted as settled.

scenarios.title: A 0.001 USDT test send against a 250.00 invoice

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: Short by 249.999, no decision yet: goes to a person (exceptions queue). Constructed: invoice set far above the real 0.001 transfer.
label.expected_reason: Received 0.001 of 250.00 USDT. A person decides: ask for the balance or accept.

scenarios.known_gap: Today the engine flags it 'Below minimum deposit: 0.001000 is below 10' (D08 from the sample deposit minimums in REQUEST_SETTINGS) and blocks it, so a person can only dismiss it, not ask for the balance or accept. It still goes to a person (no false match). Whether a deposit minimum applies to an invoice payment is a decision for Aashmiin.

scenarios.title: The same transfer reported twice

scenarios.title: Counterfeit token named "USDT"

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: The token calls itself USDT but is not Tether's contract (0xdAC17F95…1ec7): it can never pay the invoice.
label.expected_reason: Not real USDT: the token calls itself USDT but doesn't come from Tether's contract. It doesn't count.

scenarios.title: Counterfeit token with a look-alike name "ÚЅDТ", exact invoice amount

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: Cyrillic look-alike symbol, not Tether's contract; the sample invoice was set to the exact fake amount to show amount is no proof.
label.expected_reason: Not the token requested: 'ÚЅDТ' is not USDT. It doesn't count, even though the amount is exact.

scenarios.title: USDT sent on Tron for an Ethereum invoice

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: Sent on Tron; the invoice is payable on Ethereum only. Constructed: the sample invoice's Ethereum address is fictional; the Tron destination is treated as the sample business's old Tron wallet.
label.expected_reason: Paid on Tron, not Ethereum: it never reached the invoice's address. A person checks whether it landed in the business's own Tron wallet.

scenarios.known_gap: Today a hash found on another network is refused at lookup with a message and nothing is recorded on the invoice (gap K5, plan D6.2), so it never reaches the queue.

scenarios.title: Poisoned look-alike address (first 3 + last 4 equal)

transfer.label: real public transfer, not a Clearline customer

label.why: Sent to 0xbaff…f8b5, not the invoice's 0xbaf4…f8b5: a look-alike address (poisoning). Never a match; the money went to someone else. Constructed: the intended address is used as the sample invoice's address.
label.expected_reason: Not paid: sent to a look-alike address (0xbaff…f8b5), not this invoice's (0xbaf4…f8b5). Possible address poisoning.

scenarios.known_gap: Today the lookup says only 'no token transfer to the request's receiving address'; it records nothing and does not name the look-alike (D07b is off on the request path).
